text: Giorgi Sharashidze - What talk of Vice-Premiership and State Ministry status are we even having? They aren't even giving him a proper office; he won't have a staff or a secretary. I would advise Mdinaradze not to get too fixated on this office and to work remotely (28.04.2026, 12:04)

"What talk is there of a Vice-Premiership or a State Minister post? They aren't even giving him a proper office; Mdinaradze won't have a staff or even a secretary. I would advise him not to get too hung up on this office and just work remotely from home," stated Giorgi Sharashidze, an MP from the "Gakharia for Georgia" party, while discussing the creation of a State Minister position for the coordination of law enforcement agencies. According to him, appointing a "general-coordinator" will change nothing, except that it will be his "temporary satisfaction and a way to send him into retirement."

"The planned changes have nothing to do with solving the problems of our country's citizens or addressing Georgia's security issues. This is another manifestation of informal governance. 'Dream' and the 89 deputies sitting in parliament have no role other than to simply 'rubber-stamp' Ivanishvili’s decisions, which are never even coordinated with them. What talk is there of a Vice-Premiership or a State Ministry? They aren't even giving Mdinaradze a proper office; he won't have a staff or even a secretary. I would advise him not to get too fixated on this office and just work remotely from home instead."

If coordination is so important, the head of the State Security Service is not dismissed after six months for the sake of coordination. The head of the State Security Service is not appointed for a six-year term by chance—this provision in the law is not accidental. We see that in the last year, two heads of the State Security Service have already been replaced. This indicates an unstable environment and informal governance. A person was granted the rank of general in the morning and demoted to a coordinator by the evening—what special expectations should we have for this person?

"Regarding the issue of coordinatorship—it was 'Dream' itself that introduced this term. Yesterday, when one of our leaders, Giga Parulava, stated the fact at the Legal Affairs Committee meeting that they are appointing [him] as a coordinator, it caused such irritation that they criticized his vocabulary and tone. This term 'coordinator' was introduced by 'Dream,' and if they find it offensive, then they should explain where they got the term from in the first place. Therefore, when we say that the appointment of this general coordinator will change nothing except that it will simply serve as a temporary satisfaction for him before being sent into retirement, this is the reality," Sharashidze stated.

For information, the Parliament is considering a draft law through an expedited procedure, based on which the position of State Minister for the Coordination of Law Enforcement Agencies is being introduced within the Government of Georgia.
According to the draft, the Government Administration will provide material-technical and organizational support for the activities of the new State Minister.

According to Vakhtang Bachiashvili, the Parliamentary Secretary of the Government, the powers of the State Minister will be specified in a government decree, which will outline both routine and strategic responsibilities.
Mamuka Mdinaradze will be appointed to the position of State Minister for Coordination of Law Enforcement Agencies.
